subject: Math
title: Lines, functions & graphs
sub: Coordinate geometry, functions, variation, graphs of functions, travel graphs and differentiation
strategyIntro: Extended Maths is two papers of equal weight: Paper 2 (2 hours, 100 marks, no calculator) and Paper 4 (2 hours, 100 marks, calculator). Your school test may be shorter, but it is marked the same way: M marks for a correct method, A marks for the correct answer that follows, B marks for a correct result on its own.

strategy.title: Timing
points: About 1.2 minutes per mark: a 5-mark question is worth about 6 minutes.
If a question has taken twice its time, leave a gap and come back at the end.
Keep 10 minutes at the end to check answers against the question.

strategy.title: Show your working
points: Most marks are method marks. A wrong answer with clear working can still score most of the marks.
Write the calculation you are doing before the answer, e.g. 360 ÷ 12 = 30.
An answer with no working can score zero if it is wrong, and sometimes even if it is right ("show that").

strategy.title: Paper 2: no calculator
points: Practise fractions, negative numbers, standard form and surds by hand.
Leave answers exact when you can: fractions, surds, or in terms of π.
Check with a quick estimate: is the answer about the right size?

strategy.title: Paper 4: calculator
points: Give answers to 3 significant figures unless the question says otherwise; angles to 1 decimal place.
Never round partway through. Keep the full value in the calculator memory (or write 4+ figures).
Use the π button, not 3.14. Check the calculator is in degrees.

strategy.title: Answer the question
points: Read the last line again: units, form of answer ("in its simplest form", "in terms of π"), and accuracy.
"Show that" questions: every step must be written, ending with the given result.
When the question says "hence", use the previous part.

commandWords: Calculate
Work out from given facts. Show the working; usually a calculator is allowed.
Work out / Find
Get the answer by any correct method. Show working.
Write down
The answer needs little or no working: you can often read or state it.
Show that
The answer is given. Write every step clearly so the examiner can follow the logic to it.
Estimate
Round each number (usually to 1 significant figure) and calculate a rough value.
Simplify
Write in its simplest form: collect like terms, cancel common factors.
Factorise (completely)
Write as a product of factors. Completely means take out every common factor.
Expand
Multiply out the brackets.
Solve
Find the value(s) of the unknown that make the equation or inequality true.
Sketch
Show the shape and key features (intercepts, turning points), not plotted accurately.
Describe fully
For a transformation: name it and give every detail (centre, angle, direction, scale factor, vector or mirror line).
Hence
Use the result you have just found to answer this part.
Give your answer in its simplest form
Cancel fractions and ratios fully; simplify surds.
quizIntro: Quick calculations and concept checks. Do each one on paper first, then pick. The wrong options are common mistakes, so if you got one, read the working in the explanation.
flashIntro: Methods, rules and formulas. Say the rule out loud (or write it down) with an example before you tap, then check you remembered every step.

flashcards.back: (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁): change in y over change in x. Uphill left to right is positive.
m is the gradient, c is the y-intercept (where the line crosses the y-axis).
Average the coordinates: ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).
Pythagoras: √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²).
Have the same gradient. y = 3x − 1 is parallel to y = 3x + 5.
Gradients multiply to −1, so m₂ = −1/m₁ (flip and change sign). Perpendicular to gradient 2/3 is −3/2.

flashcards.front: Equation of a line through a point with gradient m
flashcards.back: Substitute the point into y = mx + c to find c, or use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
Make y the subject: y = −1.5x + 4. Gradient −1.5, y-intercept 4.
Find the midpoint of AB, find the perpendicular gradient, then the equation of the line through the midpoint with that gradient.
f(x) = 2x + 1 and f: x ↦ 2x + 1 mean the same. f(3) means substitute x = 3: f(3) = 7.
Do g first, then f: fg(x) = f(g(x)). Order matters: fg is usually not the same as gf.
Write y = f(x), swap x and y, then rearrange to make y the subject. That is f⁻¹(x).
It undoes f: f⁻¹(f(x)) = x. Its graph is the reflection of the graph of f in the line y = x.
Set the expression equal to k and solve the equation.
Domain: the input values allowed. Range: the output values produced.
You cannot divide by zero: 1/(x − 2) needs x ≠ 2. You cannot square root a negative number.
Apply f twice: substitute f(x) into f. If f(x) = 3x + 2, ff(x) = 3(3x + 2) + 2 = 9x + 8.

flashcards.front: y is directly proportional to x
flashcards.back: y ∝ x, so y = kx. The graph is a straight line through the origin.

flashcards.front: y is inversely proportional to x
flashcards.back: y = k/x. As x doubles, y halves.

flashcards.front: y is proportional to the square of x
flashcards.back: y = kx². If x is doubled, y is multiplied by 2² = 4.

flashcards.front: y is proportional to the square root of x
flashcards.back: y = k√x.

flashcards.front: y is inversely proportional to the square of x
flashcards.back: y = k/x². If x is doubled, y is divided by 4.

flashcards.front: y is proportional to the cube of x
flashcards.back: y = kx³. If x is doubled, y is multiplied by 8.
1. Write the equation with k. 2. Substitute the given pair to find k. 3. Rewrite the formula with the value of k. 4. Use it to answer.

flashcards.front: Spotting the type of variation in words
flashcards.back: "proportional to" → multiply by k; "inversely proportional to" → k divided by it. Watch for "square", "cube", "square root".

flashcards.front: Shape of y = ax² + bx + c
flashcards.back: Parabola. a > 0: U-shaped with a minimum. a < 0: ∩-shaped with a maximum. Symmetrical about the vertical line through the turning point.
S-shaped curve through the origin, rising from bottom left to top right (a negative x³ term flips it).
Two separate branches (a hyperbola). Asymptotes are the axes x = 0 and y = 0: the curve gets close but never touches them.
Passes through (0, 1), rises more and more steeply. As x becomes very negative it approaches the x-axis (asymptote y = 0) but never touches it.
Read the x-coordinates where the curve crosses the x-axis.

flashcards.front: Solving a related equation with a line
flashcards.back: Rearrange the new equation so one side is the plotted function; the other side is the line to draw. Read the x-coordinates where they cross.

flashcards.front: Gradient of a curve at a point
flashcards.back: Draw a tangent touching the curve at that point, pick two points far apart on it, and work out rise ÷ run.

flashcards.front: Plotting a curve from a table
flashcards.back: Plot each point accurately with a small cross, then join with a smooth freehand curve (no ruler, no straight segments).
A maximum or minimum point on a curve, where the gradient is zero.
Speed. A horizontal line means stationary; a steeper line means faster.
Acceleration (m/s²). A negative gradient is deceleration; a horizontal line is constant speed.
Distance travelled. Split the area into rectangles, triangles and trapezia.
Total distance ÷ total time, including any time spent stopped.
Change in speed ÷ time taken. From 4 m/s to 16 m/s in 6 s: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 m/s².
The speed is changing. Find the speed at an instant from the gradient of the tangent.
Divide by 60: 20 minutes = 20/60 = ⅓ hour. Use hours when the speed is in km/h.

flashcards.front: Area of a trapezium on a speed–time graph
flashcards.back: ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × width. The parallel sides are usually the two time lengths at the top and bottom.
Multiply by the power, then reduce the power by 1: d/dx(axⁿ) = naxⁿ⁻¹. y = 4x³ → dy/dx = 12x².
A constant differentiates to 0. kx differentiates to k (e.g. 5x → 5).
The gradient function: it gives the gradient of the curve at any value of x.
Differentiate, then substitute the x-coordinate of the point into dy/dx.
Solve dy/dx = 0 to find x; substitute into the ORIGINAL equation to find y.
Find d²y/dx² (differentiate again). Positive → minimum; negative → maximum. Or check the sign of dy/dx just either side.

flashcards.front: Equation of a tangent at a point
flashcards.back: Find the gradient m from dy/dx at that x, then use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
Rewrite as a power first: 1/x² = x⁻², which differentiates to −2x⁻³ = −2/x³.

quiz.q: What is the gradient of the line through (2, 5) and (6, −3)?
What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to y = 4x − 1?
quiz.why: Negative reciprocal of 4 is −¼. Check: 4 × (−¼) = −1.

quiz.q: Find the midpoint of (−3, 4) and (7, 10).
quiz.why: ((−3 + 7)/2, (4 + 10)/2) = (2, 7). (5, 3) is half the difference, not the average.

quiz.q: Find the length of the line from (1, 2) to (7, 10).
quiz.why: √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10. Adding 6 + 8 = 14 is wrong.

quiz.q: What is the gradient of the line 3x + 2y = 12?
quiz.why: 2y = −3x + 12 → y = −1.5x + 6. Gradient −3/2. (6 is the y-intercept.)

quiz.q: f(x) = 3x − 5. Find f(−2).
f(x) = x² and g(x) = x + 3. Find fg(2).
quiz.why: g first: g(2) = 5. Then f(5) = 25. Doing f first gives gf(2) = 7.

quiz.q: f(x) = (x + 4)/3. Find f⁻¹(x).
quiz.why: y = (x + 4)/3, swap: x = (y + 4)/3 → 3x = y + 4 → y = 3x − 4. The reciprocal (3/(x + 4)) is not the inverse.

quiz.q: f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x². Find gf(x).
quiz.why: f first, then square: (2x + 1)² = 4x² + 4x + 1. 2x² + 1 is fg(x).

quiz.q: Which value of x must be excluded from the domain of f(x) = 5/(2x − 3)?
quiz.why: The denominator 2x − 3 = 0 when x = 1.5, and you cannot divide by zero.

quiz.q: y is proportional to x². y = 12 when x = 2. Find y when x = 5.
quiz.why: 12 = k × 4 → k = 3. y = 3 × 25 = 75. 30 comes from treating it as y = kx.

quiz.q: y is inversely proportional to x. y = 6 when x = 4. Find y when x = 3.
quiz.why: k = xy = 24. y = 24 ÷ 3 = 8. Smaller x → bigger y.

quiz.q: y is inversely proportional to x². What happens to y when x is halved?
quiz.why: y = k/x². Halving x makes x² a quarter, so y is multiplied by 4.

quiz.q: p is proportional to √q. p = 10 when q = 16. Find p when q = 36.
The time t to fill a pool is inversely proportional to the number of pumps n. Which formula is correct?
quiz.why: Inversely proportional → t = k/n: more pumps, less time.

quiz.q: Which statement about the graph of y = 2ˣ is true?
options: It has an asymptote at x = 0
quiz.why: 2⁰ = 1, so it crosses the y-axis at (0, 1). Its asymptote is y = 0, not x = 0.

quiz.q: The graph of y = x² − 4x + 1 is drawn. Which line should you draw to solve x² − 4x − 2 = 0?
quiz.why: x² − 4x − 2 = 0 → x² − 4x + 1 = 3 (add 3 to both sides). So draw y = 3.

quiz.q: Which graph has both axes as asymptotes?
quiz.why: y = 4/x is undefined at x = 0 and never reaches y = 0. y = 4ˣ only has y = 0 as an asymptote.

quiz.q: What is the line of symmetry of y = x² − 6x + 5?
quiz.why: Roots are x = 1 and x = 5 ((x − 1)(x − 5)); halfway between them is x = 3. Or x = −b/2a = 6/2 = 3.

quiz.q: A tangent to a curve at x = 2 passes through (1, 3) and (4, 12). Estimate the gradient of the curve at x = 2.
quiz.why: Gradient of the tangent = (12 − 3) ÷ (4 − 1) = 9 ÷ 3 = 3.

quiz.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 24 m/s in 8 s. What is its acceleration?
quiz.why: Acceleration = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 m/s².

quiz.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 24 m/s in 8 s. How far does it travel in those 8 seconds?
quiz.why: Area of the triangle = ½ × 8 × 24 = 96 m. 192 m forgets the ½.

quiz.q: On a distance–time graph, what does a horizontal line show?
quiz.why: Distance from the start is not changing, so the object is not moving.

quiz.q: An object moves at 10 m/s for 30 s, then decelerates uniformly to rest in 5 s. How far does it travel altogether?
quiz.why: Rectangle 30 × 10 = 300 m, plus triangle ½ × 5 × 10 = 25 m: total 325 m.

quiz.q: A cyclist travels 12 km in 40 minutes. What is the average speed in km/h?
quiz.why: 40 minutes = ⅔ hour. 12 ÷ ⅔ = 18 km/h.

quiz.q: Differentiate y = 5x⁴ − 3x + 7.
Find the gradient of y = x² − 6x at x = 4.
Find the x-coordinate of the turning point of y = x² + 8x − 3.
Differentiate y = 6/x.
y = x³ − 12x has a turning point at x = 2. What type is it?
quiz.why: dy/dx = 3x² − 12, d²y/dx² = 6x = 12 at x = 2. Positive → minimum. dy/dx = 0 only tells you it is a turning point.

examIntro: Paper 2 / Paper 4 style. [No calculator] questions are Paper 2; [Calculator] questions are Paper 4. Write full working first, then open the mark scheme: M1 = method mark, A1 = accuracy mark (correct answer from correct working), B1 = mark for a correct result on its own. Give yourself one mark per point you got.

exam.q: [No calculator] A line passes through (0, 3) and (4, 11). Find its equation.
[No calculator] A is (−2, 1) and B is (4, 9). Find (a) the midpoint of AB (b) the length of AB.
[No calculator] A is (−2, 1) and B is (4, 9). Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB. Give your answer in the form ax + by = c.
[No calculator] f(x) = 5 − 2x. (a) Find f(−3). (b) Solve f(x) = 13.
[No calculator] f(x) = 2x − 1 and g(x) = x² + 1. (a) Find gf(x), giving your answer in its simplest form. (b) Find f⁻¹(x).
[No calculator] f(x) = 3x + 2 and g(x) = 1/(x − 1), x ≠ 1. (a) Find g(3). (b) Find fg(x) as a single fraction. (c) Solve ff(x) = 47.
[No calculator] y is directly proportional to x. y = 18 when x = 6. Find y when x = 11.
[Calculator] y is inversely proportional to the square of (x + 1). y = 5 when x = 3. (a) Find y in terms of x. (b) Find y when x = 7.

[Calculator] The distance, d metres, that a stone falls is proportional to the square of the time, t seconds. It falls 20 m in 2 s. (a) Find a formula for d in terms of t. (b) How far does it fall in 3.5 s? (c) How long does it take to fall 180 m?
[No calculator] For y = x² − 2x − 3: (a) find y when x = −2 and when x = 1. (b) Use the graph (or the equation) to write down the solutions of x² − 2x − 3 = 0.
[No calculator] The graph of y = x² − 2x − 3 is drawn for −2 ≤ x ≤ 4. (a) Find the equation of the straight line you should draw to solve x² − 3x − 2 = 0. (b) Estimate the solutions.
points: M1: x² − 3x − 2 = 0 rearranged to x² − 2x − 3 = x − 1
M1: line drawn and intersections read
exam.note: Exact values are (3 ± √17)/2 = −0.56 and 3.56; graph readings within about 0.1 score.

exam.q: [Calculator] y = x + 4/x for 0.5 ≤ x ≤ 5. (a) Find y when x = 0.5, x = 1 and x = 5. (b) Write down the coordinates of the minimum point. (c) By drawing a suitable line on the graph, solve x + 4/x = 4.5.
[No calculator] A runner runs 6 km in 25 minutes. Find the average speed in km/h.

[No calculator] A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to 20 m/s in 10 s. It travels at 20 m/s for 30 s, then decelerates uniformly to rest in 15 s. (a) Find the acceleration in the first 10 s. (b) Find the total distance travelled.

[Calculator] A train accelerates uniformly from 12 m/s to 30 m/s in 45 s. It then decelerates uniformly to rest in 60 s. (a) Find the acceleration. (b) Find the total distance travelled. (c) Find the average speed for the whole 105 s in km/h.
[No calculator] The curve y = x³ − 4x + 2 passes through (2, 2). Find (a) the gradient of the curve at (2, 2) (b) the equation of the tangent at (2, 2).
[No calculator] y = x³ − 3x² − 9x + 5. Find the coordinates of the two turning points and determine whether each is a maximum or a minimum.
points: M1: d²y/dx² = 6x − 6 (or sign of dy/dx either side)
